rationale.progressive-disclosure: CHOSEN. Kernel composite 6.856, margin 4.293, high confidence, autonomy eligible. One collapsed row per profession family carrying a plain-language consequence line and a single 'Review this' control; expanding reveals the held pages with their evidence grades and one 'Approve for use' action. Lowest human_cognitive_load of the two (0.25) and highest legibility_of_consequence (0.85): the owner sees WHICH coworker is affected and WHAT it costs them before seeing any doctrine detail. No reject control, because the hold already is the rejection until someone acts — offering 'Reject' would imply a state the substrate does not have.
rationale.flat-list: REJECTED. Kernel composite 2.564. Rendering every held page for every family expanded, each with its own approve control, scores worst on human_cognitive_load (0.8) and scores NEGATIVE against 'Preserve the model; disclose complexity progressively' (-0.055 vs +0.054). It also fragments one governance act into per-page approvals, when the unit the operator actually reasons about is the family — approving 'security' as a craft area, not six individual pages.

notes: BI-5F3BFD13, EP-413F2602 Objective 2. Section renders nothing at all when no material is held (HeldMaterialList returns null), so on an install with no high-stakes hold the /coworker-decisions/review first viewport is unchanged and default-visible words do not grow — the common case costs zero. Copy is deliberately non-technical: it never says draft/candidate/promotionState, it says the coworker 'falls back to general platform doctrine instead of its own craft judgement'. Colour is --dpf-* tokens only (surface-1, border, text, muted, warning, success, danger); no hardcoded hex and no *-gray-* utilities. The measured-sweep path was not used: the shell route needs the served DOM on the Contributor preview, and this change is additive-and-empty on any install without held material, so the sweep would measure an unchanged route.
